title: Plan deserialization strictness
description: Every deserializable struct that parses an operator's plan refuses a field the model does not define. The paths named here are the operator-authored surface: src/plan.rs carries the flow, its steps and their locators and expectations, and src/sandbox.rs carries the sandbox block. One module deserializes outside that surface and is outside the bound rather than exempt by name: src/inference.rs reads provider responses, where leniency is correct because a vendor adding a field must not break Tinman. src/skill.rs is inside the bound: it reads the skill Tinman itself ships, compiled in from assets, which is a document this project authors and so is held to the same strictness as a plan. Discharged by the deserialization-strictness checker in verification support, which reads the derive attributes on each deserializable type under the named paths. Attested by the @contract scenario in features/harness-plan.feature.
rationale: A plan whose step carried a field the model does not define parsed, ran, asserted nothing and exited zero. Tinman exists so that a claim about a program is checked rather than believed, and an assertion that disappears while the suite reports success is that promise inverted, landing on the operator's own test suite rather than on this one. When this contract was authored on 2026-07-29, one of the deserializable types under these paths denied unknown fields; the attesting scenario owns that count now and reddens when it slips. Bounding the modules rather than listing the types is what covers the step or locator a later feature adds, since a type added to a plan is exactly where the next silent drop would hide. An exemption belongs in exemptTypes with a reason, so leniency is always a decision somebody made rather than an attribute nobody wrote.
